svg.text: claudia creates — a slide, its layout and its template (E10.4, E10.5; branch real-world-docs)
For review before any code. Content is invented. A slide is its content in the slots of a layout; the layout and everything that repeats come from the presentation's template.
A · A slide shows where it comes from
The layout chip in the bar names the slide's layout; the line above the slide names the template.
Empty slots show their kind; what repeats on every slide (footer, number) carries a small lock.
Drop one here, or press Enter
Layout chip (also Format ▸ Layout…, Ctrl+Alt+L). Shows the layout's name; opens panel C. Beside the style picker, so the bar reads
“this text is Body text, this slide is Content and picture”. Its colour is creates' apricot: it is about the slide, not the selection.
Where the slide comes from (E10.5): template › layout. Clicking a name opens the template editor at that layout (mock-up 2).
A screen reader reads it as the slide's description: “Slide 4 of 7, layout Content and picture, template Workshop”.
An empty slot says its kind and what to do. Typing, dropping or pressing Enter fills it; a filled slot looks like any text box.
Footer and slide number keep their full colour (contrast, BITV) and carry a small lock while editing; they are not objects of the
slide but of the template. Clicking one explains this instead of selecting it (panel B). No lock in print or presentation.
A small dot on a tab: this slide differs from its layout (an object moved or resized out of its slot). The list of such slides
Not a selection: a popover says where it is defined and what can be done.
Same words in composes for a page footer from the page layout (later).
This footer comes from the template
“Kick-off workshop · March” is the footer of the template Workshop.
Every slide whose layout has a footer shows it, with its number.
The layout chip or Format ▸ Layout… (Ctrl+Alt+L). Arrow keys move, Enter applies, Esc closes.
Hovering or focusing a layout shows the slide re-flowed in it, before anything changes.
Each slot takes the content of the same kind: title to title, text to text,
picture to picture. Content without a slot of its kind stays on the slide as a free
object, and the change says so (“1 picture kept as a free object”).
Free objects never move. One undo puts everything back.
Layouts are edited in the template, not here: Template… (Ctrl+Alt+E)
